newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher, soymeal closes lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher, soymeal closes lower.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed higher on talk China recently purchased or was seeking 200,000 tonnes of optional-origin soyoil, traders said.
"There's still the talk China bought 200,000 tonnes of soyoil," a trader said.
But soymeal closed lower on fears China may be cancelling soybean and soymeal purchases following the recent slide in prices, they said.
Soyoil/soymeal spreading was noted with Rosenthal Collins a key purchaser of 1,200 lots of December soyoil and The Chicago Corp bought 1,000 lots of May soyoil, traders said.
Soy products were adjusting to Friday's plunge following the release of a bearish USDA crop production report.
Technical considerations also were cited for the gain in soyoil futures, the traders said.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December soyoil Friday closed at 11.05 points, sharply below the 20 area which is generally considered an oversold point.
The RSI for December soymeal closed Friday at 18.93 points.
Soyoil closed 0.15 to 0.37 cent per lb higher, with October up 0.33 at 22.62.
Soymeal closed unchanged to $4.00 per ton lower with October down $1.60 at $235.10.
